title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
prompt:
A sorted array of **distinct** values was rotated at some pivot (e.g. `[0,1,2,4,5,6,7]` might become `[4,5,6,7,0,1,2]`). Return its minimum element. Your algorithm must run in O(log n).

**Example 1**: `[3,4,5,1,2]` → `1`

**Example 2**: `[4,5,6,7,0,1,2]` → `0`

**Example 3**: `[11,13,15,17]` → `11` (rotated a full turn)

**Constraints**: `1 <= n <= 5000`, `-5000 <= nums[i] <= 5000`, all values distinct.
hints: A rotated array is two sorted runs glued together, and the minimum is the first element of the second run. Looking at the middle element and one endpoint, can you tell which run `mid` belongs to?
Compare `nums[mid]` with `nums[hi]`. If `nums[mid] > nums[hi]`, mid is in the left (larger) run, so the minimum lies strictly to the right; otherwise the minimum is at mid or to its left.
Use `while (lo < hi)`: `if (nums[mid] > nums[hi]) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid;` — `hi = mid` (not `mid - 1`) keeps mid as a candidate, and `nums[lo]` is the answer.

solution.explanation: Comparing `nums[mid]` against `nums[hi]` tells you whether the drop (the minimum) is right of mid or at/left of it. The minimum is never discarded — we use `hi = mid`, not `mid - 1` — so the range converges exactly onto it. Comparing with `nums[lo]` instead fails on unrotated arrays. O(log n) time, O(1) space.
